abstract.value: We present a simple framework that predicts an agent's future behavior by considering the effects that other interacting agents and entities have on them. We propose to model behavior as a sequence of tokens, each representing the state of an agent at a specific timestep. The core of our approach centers around Poly-Autoregressive models, which predict the future behavior of an agent during interaction by considering the agent's past state history and the state of other agents in the scene. In this paper, we develop the mechanics of Poly-Autoregressive (PAR) modeling and show that this framework applies without any modification to an extensive range of prediction problems that, on the surface, appear as entirely different scenarios, such as human action prediction in social situations, trajectory prediction for autonomous vehicles, and object pose prediction during hand-object interaction.

primary_area.value: applications to computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities
